Unzips into a temp dir (`restoreFilePath`), returns the list of \"safe\" files (text/plain). This is the \"import\" endpoint. Question: is this route behind auth? Need to check whether a security middleware applies. In signalk-server, security is applied via a middleware that checks `securityStrategy` — the vulnerable build might not guard `validateBackup`, while the fixed build guards it.\n\n2. `POST /skServer/restore` — with JSON/form body where keys are filenames from the safe list (e.g. `{\"settings.json\": true}`). Requires the prior validateBackup to have set `restoreFilePath` (module-level variable shared). Copies files from restoreFilePath into `app.config.configPath` (the SIGNALK_NODE_CONFIG_DIR). This is the \"apply\" endpoint. Returns 202 if restoreFilePath exists.\n\nWait — note that `restoreFilePath` is a shared module variable; `validateBackup` sets it. The apply request body: `req.body[name2]` truthy — so JSON body `{\"settings.json\": true}` works (body parser). The `/restore` route returns 202 and then copies asynchronously.\n\nNow about auth: In signalk-server, the tokensecurity strategy wraps routes. Let me check how routes are guarded. There's `app.securityStrategy.addAdminMiddleware` seen for eventsRoutingData. But most routes rely on a global middleware: in tokensecurity.js there's something that requires auth for all requests except whitelisted, when security is enabled. Actually in signalk-server, `startSecurity` etc. Let me check how the binary enables auth: ADMINUSER env var creates initial admin. Let me search for ADMINUSER in strings.\n\nAlso the evaluation says: \"On some builds the interaction you craft is accepted... on other builds the same interaction is rejected\". The vuln-normal build: `validateBackup` unauthenticated works. Other builds (patched) may reject unauthenticated import with 401. So the poc must:\n\n1. Start server with PORT, ADMINUSER, SIGNALK_NODE_CONFIG_DIR.\n2. Build a zip archive at runtime named like `signalk-poc.backup` (multipart filename must start with \"signalk-\" and end with \".backup\"), containing `settings.json` with a unique marker. Note: zip must contain `settings.json` at root of the zip (restoreFilePath = extract path). listSafeRestoreFiles filters to safeFiles: settings.json, defaults.json, security.json, package.json, baseDeltas.json, plus directories with trailing \"/\".\n3. POST /skServer/validateBackup with multipart form, no auth. Record status (import_http).\n4. Login via /login (POST JSON {username,password}) — actually `app.post([\"/login\", `${skAuthPrefix}/login`])`. skAuthPrefix is probably `/skAuth`. Response contains token. Let me check login response format: In tokensecurity, login returns `{token: ...}`? Let me check strings around the login handler.\n5. POST /skServer/restore with JSON body `{\"settings.json\": true}` and `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (or cookie?). Record status (apply_http).\n6. Wait a bit, then scan SIGNALK_NODE_CONFIG_DIR for files containing the marker. If settings.json was replaced with our content → config_replaced true, include config_content.\n7.
